ai.description: This toad reaches 7–9 cm. It is olive-grey with dark, irregular blotches and a light vertebral stripe. Key features include prominent parotoid glands and a warty, granular skin texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Bufotes latastii* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous glandular ridge (cranial crest) running behind the eye, which is absent in other toads.
ai.habitat: The Ladakh toad inhabits high-altitude arid regions, typically found near streams, marshes, and irrigation channels at elevations ranging from 2,500 to 4,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Ladakh toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for invertebrates near high-altitude streams and wetlands in the harsh Himalayan environment.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Ladakh toad is oviparous, breeding in high-altitude pools from May to July. Females lay eggs in long, gelatinous strings typical of the genus *Bufotes*.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Ladakh Toad (*Bufotes latastii*) is endemic to the high-altitude regions of Ladakh and Jammu & Kashmir, typically occurring at elevations between 2,500 and 4,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Ladakh Toad produces a series of short, rhythmic, high-pitched pulses, typically heard near high-altitude streams and marshy pools in the Himalayas.
